description: In a science club, there are two tables that can be set up to make slime. At table 1, 3 units of powder and 5 units of glue are used to make 4 units of slime. At table 2, 8 units of powder and 6 units of glue are used to make 5 units of slime. However, table 1 produces 2 units of mess while table 2 produces 4 units of mess. The science club has available 100 units of powder and 90 units of glue.  If at most 30 units of mess can be made, how many of each table should be set up to maximize the amount of slime produced?

NumTables.definition: Number of different tables for making slime

PowderUsed.definition: Amount of powder used by table i

GlueUsed.definition: Amount of glue used by table i

SlimeProduced.definition: Amount of slime produced by table i

MessProduced.definition: Amount of mess produced by table i

objective.description: "Maximize the total amount of slime produced by setting up the two tables"

constraints.description: 3 units of powder used by each table 1 setup times the number of table 1 setups plus 8 units of powder used by each table 2 setup times the number of table 2 setups should not exceed 100 units of available powder

5 units of glue used by each table 1 setup times the number of table 1 setups plus 6 units of glue used by each table 2 setup times the number of table 2 setups should not exceed 90 units of available glue

2 units of mess produced by each table 1 setup times the number of table 1 setups plus 4 units of mess produced by each table 2 setup times the number of table 2 setups should not exceed 30 units of maximum allowable mess
The number of table 1 setups and the number of table 2 setups must be non-negative
The number of table 1 setups and the number of table 2 setups must be integers
